sources: Guard relocation behind a single entry point (stage/accept pattern; check kept on every intake path)
History-based review: a removal that looks like a revert is checked against later commits in the digest
Capacity change authorised by a referenced load-test record (QA-3312) in the digest

decoys.why_not_a_defect: accept_sample no longer calls require_lot directly, but it calls stage_sample, which calls require_lot before any append. Every path (interactive accept_sample and import_rows via accept_sample) still runs the lot check; the digest shows the guard was relocated, not removed.
Looks as if a missing sample_id KeyError could escape, but the KeyError from record["sample_id"] is inside the same try block and is converted to IntakeError.

The >= looks like an off-by-one, but the check runs before the append: 499 staged samples accept one more (500 total), 500 staged samples are rejected. Exactly MAX_SAMPLES_PER_BATCH samples are allowed.
Rejects None and whitespace-only lot ids before str() conversion; a lot id of integer 0 becomes the non-empty string "0" and is a valid lot identifier, so no failing input exists.
The import works on a staged copy of the samples list and assigns it back to batch only after every row is accepted, so a rejected row leaves the batch unchanged as the docstring states.

Pre-existing flaw on an unchanged line, not in the change: at i = 0 it compares ids[0] with ids[-1] (wrap-around). check_sequential_ids([1, 2, 3]) returns False although the values strictly increase. A diff-mode reviewer must not report it; it is listed here only.
